title: RKA-Secure Signatures versus Identity-Based Encryption
summary: Naor's transform establishes the IBE-to-signature direction for RKA security; whether every RKDF class supporting RKA-secure signatures also supports RKA-secure IBE remains open.

formal_statement.body: For related-key attacks, determine whether every related-key-deriving-function (RKDF) class for which an RKA-secure signature scheme exists also supports an RKA-secure identity-based encryption scheme for the same class; equivalently, decide whether $\operatorname{RKA}[\mathrm{Sig}] \subseteq \operatorname{RKA}[\mathrm{IBE}]$.

scope.domain: Related-key-attack security relationships between digital signatures and identity-based encryption.
parameters: RKDF class — specifies the family of related-key-deriving functions under consideration
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether RKA-secure signature achievability for an RKDF class implies RKA-secure identity-based encryption achievability for the same class.

citations.label: Cryptography Secure against Related-Key Attacks and Tampering

progress.summary: The source proves that RKDF classes supporting RKA-secure IBE also support RKA-secure signatures via Naor's transform, then explicitly asks whether the converse holds.
citation_labels: Mihir Bellare et al., Cryptography Secure against Related-Key Attacks and Tampering
